The one-shot controls (implement fires them with `gate.py control`, never as entries; validation.md check 4 (6)): - `ready-deadline` — entry 6, `--timeout 120`; guard: `start` reads `opts.ready_deadline`; edit in   `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`: `opts.ready_deadline` → `INSTANCE_DEADLINE` at the wait; case   `boot_that_never_gets_ready_times_out_and_stops_its_supervisor`. With the guard gone the boot waits the 20 s   constant and the case's wall assertion (below 10 s) fails, about 20 s in, well under the 120 s bound (predicted,   unmeasured until implement fires it); `holds` = the case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. - `capture-keys` — entry 3, `--timeout 300`; guard: the key-name filter in `capture.rs` (a name outside   `[a-z_]{1,40}` counted in `other_keys`, never listed); edit: the filter's predicate replaced by `true`; case: the   unit case on an off-pattern key name. With the guard gone that name is listed in `keys` and the case's assertion   fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it). - `capture-source` — entry 3, `--timeout 300`; guard: the closed `source` words (a string outside the two wake words   reads `other`); edit: the `other` arm returns the string as given; case: the unit case on a `user` source. With   the guard gone the case reads `user` and fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it). - `wake-capture` — entry 4, `--timeout 600`; guard: the capture sign in `wake.rs` (a capture line past send 1's   mark tells the fired wake); edit: that branch's condition replaced by `false`; case: the `r3` rehearsal with a   capture line. With the guard gone the start stands to its 3 s bound, reads `wake: unfired`, and the case's   `wake-sign: capture` assertion fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it); `holds` = the case FAILED   with no TIMEOUT line (the rehearsal's own waits sit under the 12 s WITHIN, far under the binary's kill).
